SAQ01: Because actively retrieving information forces the brain to reconstruct and strengthen memory pathways, making the knowledge more durable. SAQ03: In En-ROADS, a cheap breakthrough zero-carbon energy source arrives too late to significantly reduce **cumulative emissions**, which largely determine 2100 temperature. Existing fossil infrastructure persists for decades, and many major emissions sources (like agriculture and industry) are mostly unaffected. As a result, even dramatic clean energy advances late in the century only modestly change end-of-century warming.
SAQ04: During wet-bulb heat events, the air is so humid that it’s already saturated with water vapor, eliminating the vapor-pressure gradient needed for sweat to evaporate. Without evaporation, sweat can’t remove heat from the skin. Once wet-bulb temperature approaches body temperature (~35 °C), human cooling by sweating physically stops, leading to dangerous heat buildup.
SAQ05: Methane is described as “high impact and fast” because it is **far more powerful than CO₂ at trapping heat** and has a **much shorter atmospheric lifetime** (about a decade). Cutting methane therefore produces **rapid reductions in warming**, unlike CO₂ cuts which mainly affect long-term temperature. This makes methane mitigation one of the quickest ways to slow near-term climate change.
SAQ06: In En-ROADS, increasing energy efficiency in transport and buildings helps decarbonise the energy supply mainly by shrinking the size of the problem the energy system has to solve.
